title: When it comes to Japan, China finds it hard to think straight
gist: Fletcher argues China–Japan ties have been frozen for over a year since PM Sanae Takaichi's November 2025 remark that force against Taiwan 'could constitute a survival-threatening situation', with Beijing cutting trade (including rare earth magnet exports), tourism and contact and showing no sign of softening; Japan has not backed down, Beijing may try to wait her out, and ties look 'permanently prickly' barring a summit-season thaw.

themes.theme: A year-long China–Japan freeze over Taiwan

insights.claim: China–Japan relations have been in deep freeze since November 2025, when PM Sanae Takaichi said the use of force against Taiwan 'could constitute a survival-threatening situation' for Japan, implying military intervention.
insights.speaker: Graham Fletcher
insights.so_what: Persistent bilateral freeze is a structural risk for Japanese firms with China exposure.

insights.claim: China retaliated by disrupting political contact, cultural ties, tourism and trade, including exports of rare earth magnets and dual-use items to Japan.
insights.speaker: Graham Fletcher
insights.so_what: Rare-earth magnet supply to Japanese industry (autos, electronics) is a live weaponised chokepoint; supports non-China rare-earth suppliers.

insights.claim: On 6 November 2026 China's Foreign Ministry reiterated demands that Japan 'correct the erroneous words and deeds on the Taiwan question', showing no sign of softening.
insights.speaker: Graham Fletcher
insights.so_what: No near-term easing of Chinese economic coercion against Japan.
insights.quote: correct the erroneous words and deeds on the Taiwan question

insights.claim: Beijing's intense reaction reflected a desire to establish early dominance over a new, female, hawkish leader in office under three weeks and force a backdown.
insights.speaker: Graham Fletcher
insights.so_what: Coercion is calibrated to leaders; leadership changes could shift dynamics.

insights.claim: Japan arouses particular Chinese sensitivity on Taiwan because the Qing Dynasty's 1895 defeat ceded Taiwan to Japan as a colony.
insights.speaker: Graham Fletcher
insights.so_what: Historical framing makes Japan a preferred target of Chinese pressure.

insights.claim: Recently stabilised US–China relations gave Beijing a lower-risk environment in which to punish Tokyo, and Beijing hopes to weaken Japan's defence buildup.
insights.speaker: Graham Fletcher
insights.so_what: US–China détente shifts Chinese coercion toward US allies — Japan risk premium rises even as US–China risk falls.
insights.quote: The volatile China–US relationship had recently stabilised, providing a lower risk environment in which Beijing could punish Tokyo.

insights.claim: Fletcher calls China's propaganda about resurgent Japanese militarism 'overblown and ridiculous', arguing its echo chamber is adept at targeting victims but unsuited to self-correction.
insights.speaker: Graham Fletcher
insights.so_what: Chinese policy toward Japan is unlikely to self-correct quickly.
insights.quote: Its rhetoric about resurgent militarism is overblown and ridiculous.

insights.claim: Japan has not backed down; Tokyo has calmly stood its ground while leaving the door open to dialogue.
insights.speaker: Graham Fletcher
insights.so_what: Japan's resolve signals the standoff persists.

insights.claim: Beijing may be trying to wait Takaichi out, but this is risky because, like Shinzo Abe whose mantle she inherited, she could prove durable — and Chinese pressure may strengthen her politically.
insights.speaker: Graham Fletcher
insights.so_what: A long Takaichi tenure implies durable Japan–China friction and sustained Japanese defence spending.
insights.quote: Who is to say that Beijing’s pressure campaign will not serve to strengthen her politically?

insights.claim: The East Asia Summit (16–17 November), APEC (18–19 November) and G20 (14–15 December) offer potential for initial leader rapprochement, with the EAS likelier since China's premier rather than Xi attends; otherwise no circuit-breaker is in sight.
insights.speaker: Graham Fletcher
insights.so_what: Watch for a China–Japan leaders' meeting as a catalyst for China-exposed Japanese equities (tourism, retail, autos).

insights.claim: Fletcher judges Takaichi's explicitness an unnecessary, unforced misstep, while Beijing's intransigence rules out the accommodation it claims to seek, so Japan–China ties look set to remain permanently prickly.
insights.speaker: Graham Fletcher
insights.so_what: Price in structural, not cyclical, Japan–China tension.
insights.quote: Japan–China ties look set to remain permanently prickly.
